hero.lead: Break Glass If Bored is a Roblox experience by Nebula where you smash museum objects—statues, vases, chandeliers, chess sets, and organ pipes—using physics-based destruction and over 25 weapons. Earn money from every piece you break and spend it on upgrades like pistols, shotguns, sledgehammers, laser cutters, grenades, and more exotic tools. This guide covers core gameplay mechanics, beginner progression, key systems, early strategies, and common mistakes to help you climb the leaderboards.

sections.heading: Core Mechanics & Progression Overview in Break Glass If Bored
sections.intro: Break Glass If Bored revolves around a straightforward but satisfying loop: destroy museum objects, earn cash, and reinvest your earnings into increasingly powerful weapons. Every statue, vase, chandelier, chess set, and organ pipe in the museum is destructible using physics-based breakage, meaning no two destruction sequences play out identically. This dynamic destruction system forms the core of progression—you're not grinding abstract points, but literally watching your earned upgrades shatter more of the environment.
paragraphs: The financial system drives your advancement. Each destroyed object pays out money proportional to its value and the weapon used. Early earnings fund your first weapon purchases: pistols and shotguns provide reliable damage output, while specialized tools like the sledgehammer, laser cutter, grenades, and exotic weapons like the singularity and nuke unlock as you progress. Over 25 weapons are available across the game, each suited to different destruction strategies and speed-running approaches.

The Infinite Museum structure ensures long-term content expansion. New wings and weapons are added regularly, so players always have undiscovered areas to explore. Each wing conceals at least one secret weapon—hidden upgrades tied to specific discovery challenges or environmental puzzles. The leaderboard system tracks two metrics: total glass broken and cumulative time spent in the museum halls. This dual-metric leaderboard rewards both aggressive destruction speed and consistent playtime investment.

Membership and premium perks add a secondary progression layer. Joining the official group unlocks an exclusive members' reward available in the Reception area. Roblox Premium members receive immediate access to the Force Push weapon at no in-game cost, providing a head start on momentum-based destruction tactics. These perks are optional but relevant for competitive leaderboard climbing.

sections.heading: Getting Started: Controls, First Weapons & Early Progression
sections.intro: When you first launch Break Glass If Bored, you spawn in the museum's Reception area. Use your mouse to aim and left-click to fire your starting weapon—a basic pistol. WASD moves you around the halls, spacebar jumps, and your camera follows your mouse. The goal is straightforward: destroy everything breakable to earn money, then spend it on better weapons and upgrades. Roblox Premium members start with an exclusive Force Push weapon unlocked, giving you an early advantage if you have the subscription.
paragraphs: Your first earnings come fast. Every object you smash—statues, vases, chandeliers, chess sets, organ pipes—drops money instantly. Start by targeting the smaller, easier pieces in Reception to get comfortable with aiming and the physics. Money accumulates in real time, so you can watch your balance grow as you play. Early on, focus on breaking everything in sight rather than strategy; the game rewards exploration and destruction equally.

Once you've earned your first 50–100 money (exact thresholds vary by update), open the shop menu to buy your second weapon. Most players choose the shotgun or sledgehammer next because they deal more damage and break larger objects faster, speeding up your earning rate. The laser cutter is another popular early pick because it cuts through certain materials cleanly, making breakage feel more satisfying. Avoid spending all your money at once; save enough to unlock one new weapon, then return to farming money in your current setup.

New wings and weapons are added regularly, so always check the museum layout for unfamiliar areas or weapon slots. Every wing hides a secret weapon waiting to be discovered—these free unlocks can rival paid upgrades if you find them early. To locate secrets, explore corners, rooftops, and behind large objects; look for visual clues like loose panels or glowing crevices. Finding your first secret weapon is a major confidence boost and frees up money for other priorities.

Common beginner mistakes: spending money too fast on exotic weapons before mastering the basics, ignoring secret weapons and missing free upgrades, and camping one small area instead of rotating through the museum to find higher-value targets. Objects respawn or new ones appear as you progress, so the museum never runs out of things to break. Set a goal for your first session—like reaching a specific money milestone or finding one secret—and use that to guide your early playtime.

sections.heading: Weapons & Upgrades: What to Buy First
sections.intro: Your first purchases shape your entire early game. Break Glass If Bored rewards aggressive destruction, so prioritize weapons that deal consistent damage without requiring rare resources. Pistols and shotguns are your entry points—they cost little, fire quickly, and teach you how each weapon type handles physics-based destruction.
paragraphs: Start by unlocking the pistol if you haven't already. It's affordable and lets you practice aiming and timing. Once you've earned enough from initial museum runs, move to the shotgun. The shotgun costs more but breaks larger objects in fewer shots, meaning faster money per session and quicker progression to mid-tier tools. These two weapons alone carry you through the early museum wings.

The sledgehammer represents your first significant upgrade. It's slower than firearms but delivers massive area damage, letting you destroy multiple objects in one swing. Buy it once you've saved enough capital—it accelerates your earning rate enough to justify the investment. Use it on clustered objects like chess sets or chandeliers to maximize money per second.

Don't rush into exotic weapons like grenades or laser cutters early. They cost substantially more and are designed for mid-game optimization, not starter progression. Focus on mastering the three basic archetypes—rapid-fire (pistol), spread damage (shotgun), and heavy impact (sledgehammer)—before branching into specialized tools.

If you're a Roblox Premium member, claim Force Push immediately from your free weapons. This ability pushes objects remotely, letting you break items you can't physically reach or angle toward, which solves early puzzle-like scenarios in certain wings. It has no recharge cooldown in basic form, making it uniquely powerful for exploration.

Your upgrade order should track your earning speed. Once pistol and shotgun feel slow, jump to the sledgehammer. Once the sledgehammer stops clearing rooms efficiently, check the full weapons database for the next tier—typically grenades for area control or the laser cutter for precision breaks. Never spend everything on one weapon; keep a reserve for unexpected opportunities or mid-session weapon swaps.
bullets: Shotgun: moderate cost, high damage per shot, faster progression than pistol alone
Sledgehammer: first major purchase, enables area destruction, worth the capital investment
Grenades and laser cutter: mid-game upgrades, skip until you've mastered basics
Force Push (Premium): free and infinite-use, solve early wing puzzles and hidden areas

sections.heading: Secret Weapons & Hidden Areas
sections.intro: Every museum wing in Break Glass If Bored contains a secret weapon waiting to be discovered. Rather than appearing in your shop or dropping automatically, these hidden tools are tucked away in specific locations throughout each wing—rewarding curious players who explore beyond the main destruction zones. Finding them all is part of the progression challenge and unlocks unique playstyles you won't access through standard purchases alone.
paragraphs: The museum itself expands over time. New wings and weapons are added regularly, which means the total number of secrets continues to grow. This rotating content keeps exploration meaningful even after you've mastered the early areas. Each wing is designed with its own layout and aesthetic, so the hiding spots vary—what works as a secret location in one area won't apply to another.

Exploration is incentivized not just by novelty but by genuine gameplay advantage. Secret weapons often fill niche roles or provide mechanical variety compared to standard shop purchases. Once you locate a hidden tool, it becomes available for use and upgrades just like any other weapon, so the discovery directly impacts your combat options and leaderboard performance.

For a complete wing-by-wing breakdown of where secrets hide and exactly how to unlock each one, refer to the Break Glass If Bored All Secrets guide. That dedicated resource walks through each discovery step-by-step so you don't miss any hidden weapons on your path to the top of the boards.

sections.heading: Climbing the Leaderboards & Group Rewards
sections.intro: Break Glass If Bored tracks player performance across two independent leaderboards: one for total glass broken and another for time spent exploring the museum halls. Both rankings update as you progress, letting you compete against other players worldwide. Climbing these boards requires consistent destruction and strategic weapon choices—faster breaks and higher-damage tools help you accumulate points more efficiently.
paragraphs: The Glass Broken leaderboard measures your cumulative destruction output across all museum wings. Every piece you shatter—from small vases to massive chandeliers—counts toward your total. Players aiming for top ranks typically focus on high-damage weapons and techniques that maximize destruction per session, then return regularly to extend their lead.

The Time Spent leaderboard tracks how long you remain active in the museum halls. This creates a different competitive angle: consistent play and extended sessions matter as much as raw destruction power. Some players use this leaderboard as a long-term goal, building steady progress over many visits rather than chasing peak destruction in single runs.

Joining the official Break Glass If Bored group unlocks an exclusive members' reward available in the Reception wing. This reward provides a tangible incentive to connect with the community and may offer in-game benefits tied to group participation. Check the group page for current membership perks and any time-limited bonuses.

Roblox Premium members receive the Force Push weapon at no cost, giving them an early advantage in both leaderboards. This tool offers unique destruction mechanics unavailable to free-to-play accounts, making Premium membership a consideration for players serious about competitive ranking.
bullets: Glass Broken leaderboard: ranked by total destruction across all wings
Time Spent leaderboard: ranked by cumulative hours in the museum

faq.question: How do you play Break Glass If Bored on Roblox?
faq.answer: Launch the experience and use your starting weapon to destroy museum objects—statues, vases, chandeliers, chess sets, and organ pipes.
